Financial institutions tend to keep short, restrictive hours that compete with customers’ workdays and class schedules. Implementing conversational AI in banking fills this gap by offering 24/7 service to customers without increasing operating costs. Even during open hours, AI agents reduce long wait times by answering routine questions, verifying customer identities, and even handling payment disputes.

Cost-effectiveness and improved customer experience from these automated services have made conversational AI a mainstay in banking. But chatbots spreading quickly isn’t necessarily an advantage. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau reported in 2023 that the top 10 U.S. banks had already added chatbots to their workflows, and more than a third of Americans had interacted with these bots. Yet, the CFPB also found problems with how those bots performed, demonstrating why real resolutions and clear handoffs to people matter even more.

This guide shows what conversational AI in banking is and how modern financial teams build high-volume support pipelines to bring human-level dialogue to customer interactions while securing sensitive data. We also discuss the types of artificial intelligence technology used by banks and how to measure success across various channels.

## Summary

• Conversational AI in banking uses agents that process natural language requests to provide 24/7 support to customers.

• Customers use conversational banking to quickly handle tasks, such as resolving routine queries or getting updates to pending account issues.

• Secure conversational banking systems protect financial data through strict cybersecurity protocols and by maintaining compliance with SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS.

• Operational leaders track performance across different banking chatbot use cases by measuring key metrics, such as first-contact resolution rates and escalation frequencies.

• High-impact chatbot use cases include account onboarding, payment reminders, dispute intake, and fraud alerts.

• Voice agents let customers handle phone banking in natural conversation, with faster responses across dozens of languages.

## What is conversational AI in banking?

Conversational AI in banking uses automated chat and voice systems to handle bank interactions and resolve customer queries. Instead of routing every request to a human, these AI agents only escalate issues they cannot resolve or when specifically asked to do so by a customer.

These chatbots are different from basic rules-based models that follow rigid scripts. Modern conversational banking platforms understand natural language and pull real account context. These systems handle tasks like requesting information, interpreting intent, verifying user identities, and resolving complex workflows in real time.

In short, conversational AI lets customers speak or type to their bank the same way they would to a human agent. Let's take a look at what this looks like in practice.

## What types of AI do banks use?

Financial institutions implement AI models for both customer-facing and back-office functions. While they need AI models for customer experience and support, banks also use specialized models for things like risk management and fraud detection.

These are the core technologies they use to optimize workflows:

• Conversational AI: Conversational AI, built on natural language processing (NLP), powers customer-facing roles through real-time voice and chat interactions. For example, ElevenAgents implemented at banks uses NLP to interpret user intent and execute routine transactions across channels.

• Generative AI: Generative AI also uses NLP but can ingest other types of data, such as images. Gen AI agents speed up internal research, analyze complex documents, and draft reports for banking staff. Administrative use cases are distinct from customer-facing tasks like powering chatbots.

• Machine learning: ML models analyze transactional history and historical data to identify potential fraud in real time and execute risk scoring on demand. These algorithms also monitor network activity continuously to identify anomalies and block suspicious transactions.

## Conversational AI vs. chatbots vs. IVR in banking

Banks have used phone menus and scripted chatbots for years. Conversational AI takes a different approach, building out a more natural way of interacting with banking systems.

Learn more about IVR and how an AI voice agent differs from traditional options. For most banks, the practical path is conversational AI for open-ended requests, with clear handoffs and guardrails in place.

## Conversational banking versus traditional banking

Modern financial institutions have faced increasing competition from fintech companies that successfully reduced friction and transformed static customer service by automating services. Many also provided 24/7 support via chat with humans and AI agents.

Operations leaders at large financial institutions are catching up and capturing the full benefits of AI in banking by implementing automated workflows. These changes prioritize customer convenience while reducing the cost of running contact centers.

Here’s how modern conversational banking compares to traditional systems.

Delivers 24/7 support across voice and digital chat channels
